method: Direct centred-window crop (no resampling) from the native-resolution PGDA average-Earth-visibility raster. This product is computed by PGDA from LOLA topography using the full Earth disc against the local terrain horizon (not a bare geometric point test), over an 18.6-year lunar nutation cycle at hourly timestep (PGDA products/69, Mazarico et al. 2011). This pipeline does not independently recompute Earth visibility from ephemeris + a per-pixel horizon raycast for the regional layer: web/public/data/ephem/ephem.bin is an unresolved Git-LFS pointer in this environment (same blocker noted elsewhere in the project), and no Tier-A horizon masks exist for a region-wide grid. Known limitation carried from the source: Earth is counted visible if any part of its disc is unobscured, which is slightly optimistic relative to a DSN-station-only link study.
nodata_encoding: fully transparent alpha channel (RGBA PNG); never encoded as a visible class or value

source.citation: Mazarico, E., et al. (2011), Icarus, Vol. 211, pp. 1066-1081, doi:10.1016/j.icarus.2010.10.030
source.name: Average Earth visibility, 85S-90S, 60 m/px
source.value_meaning: fraction of time any part of the Earth disc is above the local LOLA-topography horizon, in [0, 1], averaged hourly over an 18.6-year lunar nutation cycle
